title: The uneventful twelve-week
stem: 54-year-old man, routine 12-week review. Started compounded semaglutide for ‘longevity and metabolic hygiene’. No diabetes. He says it is going well and he has no questions.

meds: compounded semaglutide 1.0 mg weekly, from a suburban compounding pharmacy, lot not recorded

hidden.exposure.molecule: Compounded semaglutide. He thinks it is ‘the same as Ozempic’. Salt unknown. No lot card.
hidden.exposure.dose: 1.0 mg weekly Fridays. Titrated 0.25→0.5→1.0 over 8 weeks. No missed doses.
hidden.exposure.source: Local compounding pharmacy. Paid cash. No TGA-registered branded product. Reconstituted by pharmacy.
hidden.indication.off_label: Wants to ‘live to 90 and stay sharp’. BMI was 29.8. No T2DM. Off-label explicitly.
hidden.indication.consent: Verbal only. No written off-label discussion on file.
hidden.efficacy.weight_rate: 8.6 kg in 12 weeks (9.1% TBW). Last 4 weeks 0.4 kg/week. Not rapid.
hidden.efficacy.appetite: Food noise gone. Skips lunch most days without noticing.
hidden.composition.protein: Estimates 50–60 g/day. Mostly coffee until 14:00. ~0.6 g/kg.
hidden.composition.resistance: Walks the dog. Has not lifted since starting. Used to do some bench twice a week.
hidden.composition.strength: Stairs fine. Has not noticed weakness. Jumpers looser in the shoulders.
hidden.composition.lean: Face thinner. No DXA. Mild hair shedding last month.
hidden.gi.nausea: Queasy Friday night after injection, eats a smaller dinner, gone by Saturday. Fluids fine. CTCAE G1.
hidden.gi.intake: Calories down because of appetite, fluids 2 L. Urine normal.
hidden.hepato.biliary: No RUQ, no pale stool, no jaundice.
hidden.psych.mood: Mood steady. Slightly flatter about restaurants, which he considers a feature.
hidden.plan.safety_net: He has no idea what would be an emergency.

gold.summary: Off-label compounded semaglutide, expected G1 nausea, 9% loss with inadequate protein and no resistance training.
must_address: G1 nausea expected — do not stop

idiot_moves.why: full body panel with no finding

title: Tuesday night RUQ
stem: 47-year-old woman, 16-week review, branded tirzepatide for weight and ‘healthspan’. She mentions a bad night after takeaway on Tuesday but is mainly here for a dose increase.

hidden.exposure.dose: 2.5→5→7.5→10. Last increase 3 weeks ago. Wants 12.5 today.
hidden.exposure.source: Brand, pharmacy, PBS not covering — private.
hidden.indication.off_label: Started for BMI 32. Now talking longevity. Off-label relative to diabetes; obesity indication exists in some labels — she is using it as healthspan.
hidden.efficacy.weight_rate: 12.6 kg / 16 weeks (13.9%). Last 4 weeks 1.4 kg/week after she ‘stopped bothering with dinner’.
hidden.gi.pain_map: Tuesday 21:00 colicky RUQ after fried chicken, lasted 3 hours, paced the kitchen, no fever. Residual ache yesterday.
hidden.hepato.biliary: That Tuesday pain. Stool was pale once on Wednesday. Urine darker that night. No jaundice seen. Fatty food trigger.
hidden.hepato.pancreas: Pain was colicky RUQ, not constant through to back. She could sit. Not pancreatitis pattern.
hidden.plan.safety_net: She thought it was indigestion from the drug.

gold.summary: Biliary colic after 1.4 kg/week loss on tirzepatide. Do not uptitrate.

idiot_moves.why: continue without ultrasound after pale stool + RUQ
labelling biliary colic as expected GI AE

title: I thought it was the dose
stem: 61-year-old man. Walk-in between scheduled reviews. Started branded semaglutide 2.4 mg for obesity; he now frames it as longevity. He looks uncomfortable in the waiting room.

hidden.exposure.dose: On 2.4 for 8 weeks. Last injection 2 days ago.
hidden.indication.off_label: Originally obesity. He reads longevity forums. Still on-label obesity; he calls it both.
hidden.efficacy.weight_rate: 19.6 kg in 20 weeks. Last month slower.
hidden.gi.nausea: Vomiting since last night, cannot keep water this morning.
hidden.gi.pain_map: Severe constant epigastric pain radiating to the back for 10 hours. Leaning forward. Cannot get comfortable. 8/10.
hidden.gi.intake: Nothing kept down. Last urine hours ago, small.
hidden.hepato.pancreas: This is the pain. Prior ‘sensitive stomach’ only. No alcohol binge. Classic pancreatitis pattern.
hidden.psych.si: No. He is frightened, not depressed.
hidden.examine: Tender epigastrium, no peritonism, no jaundice, dry mucosa, HR 104.

gold.summary: Acute pancreatitis pattern on semaglutide. ED now. Hold drug. Not a titration problem.
must_address: do not give antiemetic and send home

title: Food just sits there
stem: 39-year-old woman, 9-week review. Branded semaglutide for off-label longevity (BMI 27, euglycaemic, APOE4 heterozygote — she brought papers). She has been ‘unable to eat properly’ for a fortnight.

hidden.exposure.molecule: Semaglutide branded 1.7. She increased herself from 1.0 two weeks early because ‘the food noise came back’.
hidden.exposure.dose: Self-accelerated titration. Last dose 3 days ago.
hidden.indication.off_label: Longevity. BMI 27. No obesity indication. Written blog-consent only.
hidden.gi.nausea: Vomiting. Last night vomited food from yesterday lunch, recognisable pasta.
hidden.gi.gastroparesis: Yes. Food sits. Early satiety after a few bites. Vomiting undigested food 12–24 h later.
hidden.gi.pain_map: Bloat and fullness, not an acute pancreas/biliary pattern.
hidden.gi.intake: Sips. Two glasses yesterday. Standing black spots this morning.
hidden.renal.volume: Urine once yesterday, dark. Dizzy. No SGLT2.
hidden.examine: Orthostatic HR 96→118, dry tongue, mildly distended but soft abdomen.

gold.summary: Self-uptitrated semaglutide; gastroparesis with volume depletion. Hold. Fluids. Creatinine. Not metoclopramide-and-continue.
must_address: ED if cannot keep fluids / anuria / worsening pain

idiot_moves.why: continue through delayed emptying and oliguria

title: I don't enjoy anything
stem: 45-year-old man, 10-week review. Off-label semaglutide for longevity (physician-parent, self-referred). Weight is ‘on track’. He is quieter than the last visit.

hidden.exposure.dose: Stable 1.0 for 6 weeks. No missed doses.
hidden.composition.protein: 90 g/day. Still lifting 3x/week. This part is actually good.
hidden.gi.nausea: Minimal, G1 first fortnight only, gone.
hidden.psych.mood: Anhedonia 3 weeks. Stopped seeing friends. Work is mechanical. ‘Nothing is rewarding, not just food.’ Sleep intact. No mania.
hidden.psych.si: Passive SI: ‘wouldn’t mind not waking’. No plan, no intent, no means rehearsal. Would not tell his partner. Shame.
hidden.plan.safety_net: He did not know mood was on the label.

gold.summary: New anhedonia and passive SI on GLP-1. Composition is fine. This is a psych safety visit, not a dose visit.
must_address: do not dismiss as appetite suppression working
safety plan, inform support person if he agrees
hold vs continue is shared — hold is defensible

idiot_moves.why: cease drug and no safety plan

title: A curtain over the lower vision
stem: 58-year-old woman. T2DM on metformin plus off-label ‘extra’ semaglutide she calls her longevity dose. She mentions a visual episode yesterday and wants to know if she can still drive to the coast this weekend.

hidden.exposure.molecule: Ozempic 1.0. She calls 0.5 the diabetes dose and 1.0 the longevity dose — same pen.
hidden.indication.off_label: Mixed: T2DM on-label, the ‘extra’ framing is longevity.
hidden.eye.field: Yesterday AM: sudden painless grey curtain over the lower field of the RIGHT eye. Still there, slightly better. No flashes as a prelude, no trauma. Left eye normal. No eye pain, no headache at onset.
hidden.eye.retinopathy: Last screen 14 months, mild NPDR. No photocoagulation. This is not a floater story.
hidden.plan.safety_net: She was going to wait until Monday optometrist.

gold.summary: Acute painless monocular inferior field defect on GLP-1. Same-day ophthalmology. Not Specsavers, not ‘retinopathy routine’.
must_address: NAION is the signal you are being tested on
retinopathy screening being overdue is a separate issue, not the diagnosis

title: Research peptide, same thing
stem: 32-year-old man. First presentation to this clinic. He has been injecting ‘sema’ from a telegram vendor for longevity. He has a fever after the last injection and wants a prescription so he can ‘do it properly’.

meds: unlabelled vial in his bag, white powder, bacteriostatic water

hidden.exposure.molecule: Vendor labelled ‘semaglutide 5 mg’. No COA he trusts. Lyophilised, he reconstituted in his kitchen.
hidden.exposure.dose: He uses insulin syringe units. Thinks he is taking ‘1 mg’. Arithmetic is inconsistent. Last injection yesterday left lower abdomen.
hidden.exposure.source: Grey. Telegram. Crypto payment. Not a compounding pharmacy. Not a licensed product.
hidden.product.site: 4 cm erythematous tender nodule at last site. Warm. Red streak 3 cm. Fever 38.4 started overnight. One older nodule from week 3, still firm.
hidden.product.dosing_error: Possible mg/mL confusion. He has had two days of severe nausea after a ‘big’ dose three weeks ago.

gold.summary: Unlicensed peptide, likely bacterial site infection. Stop the vial. Treat the infection. Do not convert this into a branded titration today.
must_address: manage cellulitis/abscess — do not dose-adjust a telegram peptide
fever after injection is infection until proven otherwise
do not write a convenience prescription in the same visit without cooling off and indication review

idiot_moves.why: same-day Wegovy start on a febrile cellulitis
advise to use smaller units of the same vial

title: Neck lump, sister’s thyroid
stem: 50-year-old woman, 24-week review. Liraglutide 3.0 mg for weight; she is here because a longevity clinic continued it. She mentions a new hoarse voice and that her sister ‘had thyroid cancer’.

hidden.indication.off_label: Obesity start; longevity clinic took over. Off-label relative to that clinic’s framing.
hidden.indication.contraindication: Sister: total thyroidectomy at 34. Patient does not know histology. Sister was told ‘a rare type’ and had genetic testing the patient never completed.
hidden.endocrine.mtc: Hoarse 3 weeks. Small right anterior neck lump she noticed while putting on a necklace. No pain. Occasional watery stools 4–5/day for a month — she blamed the GLP-1.
hidden.examine: 1.5 cm firm right thyroid-region nodule, non-tender. Voice breathy.

gold.summary: Hoarseness, thyroid-region mass, sister with ‘rare’ thyroid cancer — boxed-warning territory. Stop. Endocrine/thyroid workup. Do not assume papillary.
investigations: do not start calcitonin-as-theatre without specialist
must_address: neck mass + hoarseness is not ‘Ozempic voice’
watery diarrhoea is not automatically the usual GI AE here

idiot_moves.why: reassure FHx is probably papillary and continue 3.0
increase fibre for watery stools and ignore the neck
